name: net-b4-input-frames
title: Netcode B4: networked input layout, InputFrame, redundant client inputs, server jitter buffer
issue: Design: C:/Method Notes Obsidian/orchestrator/proposals/netcode-runtime-design.md (N1-N15 ACCEPTED): read the whole document, the sections for this stage and the stage table row, then the MERGED code: n2net (transports, SecureTransport, channels, the network simulator and its tests), N2Server, B1 (NetworkObject, world/server/client classes, fingerprint) and B2 (field replication: .Replicated(), codecs, delta vs acked baseline, NetworkTransform) in engine/src/network, A2 (simulation clock, fixed tick, StepTicks, TickOptions), and the existing network docs page. Follow the security rules of the design (bounded counts and sizes before allocation, rate limits, authority checks, no client-controlled allocation). The web build must still compile (n2net core is compiled for web; native sockets are not). Nothing builds locally: re-read every edit twice and trace identifiers. SCOPE (stage B4 only): (1) an input layout declaration (a small schema of named axes/buttons/vectors with bit widths and quantisation, declared in C++ and from Lua, registered in the fingerprint from B1 so client and server must agree) and the InputFrame type (tick, sequence, packed payload); (2) client side: sample the local input each fixed tick into an InputFrame, keep a bounded ring of unacked frames, send each datagram with the last N frames (redundancy, N from settings) on the unreliable channel so loss does not lose inputs, acks from the server trim the ring; (3) server side: per client jitter buffer keyed by tick (bounded depth), duplicate/old/too-far-future frames rejected, a configurable input delay target, behaviour when an input is missing (repeat last input N ticks then neutral input; counters exposed), rate limit and size cap per client per second, authority: input is applied ONLY for the client's own controlled object(s) as assigned by the server; (4) a server API for the game to read the input of the controlled object for the current tick (C++ and Lua), deterministic given the same frames; (5) tests on the simulator: loss and reorder do not drop inputs thanks to redundancy, jitter buffer ordering and bounds, flood rejected, missing input policy, quantisation round trip, determinism of encode; (6) docs true against the code. NO prediction/reconciliation here (B6). Nothing builds locally for the engine; CI (12 checks) is the test; expect fix rounds; re-read every edit twice (CMake/YAML/C++ syntax); NEVER call a stateful function (RNG etc.) twice in one argument list or operator expression (unspecified evaluation order); NEVER run taskkill or kill other processes; verify every docs sentence against the CODE; no attribution lines on commits or PRs (no Co-Authored-By, no Generated-with footer); GitHub only via the wrapper; before your final push merge origin/master into the branch if it moved; your FINAL message must be a real report (PR number, head sha, what you did, deviations), never a single word.
acceptance: Input layout schema in the fingerprint; InputFrame encode/decode bounded
Redundant sends and acks; server jitter buffer with bounds and missing-input policy
Input applied only to the client own controlled object; rate/size limits
Simulator tests, docs true, CI green
notes: Reviewer (security): every count/size bounded, clients cannot drive objects they do not control, ring/jitter-buffer memory bounded under flood, tick wraparound, quantisation round trip, Lua layout validation, compile-level correctness, web build.
